name: What should a custom home builder quote include in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What items should be listed in a custom home estimate so there are no surprises?
mainEntity.text: What items should be listed in a custom home estimate so there are no surprises?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong custom home proposal should be specific enough to compare against other bids. It should identify site work, demolition if needed, grading, foundation, framing, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, insulation, drywall, cabinetry, tile, flooring, fixtures, and exterior finishes. It should also list allowances for items that are not fully selected yet, plus exclusions and assumptions. In Los Angeles, quotes should also make clear whether permits, engineering, utility work, and landscaping are included. Without that detail, homeowners can underestimate the true project cost and discover gaps after construction begins. A transparent quote makes it easier to manage scope, compare builders, and control change orders.
acceptedAnswer.description: A complete quote should show site work, foundation, framing, MEP systems, finishes, allowances, permits, contingency, and exclusions. If a proposal does not separate hard costs from allowances and exclusions, it is hard to compare or trust.
